Pre-emptor opposite party Nos. 1-5 as petitioners filed the aforesaid pre-emption case against the petitioners and vendor opposite party No. 6 under section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act on the allegation that they purchased 10 decimals of land of the suit plot from opposite party No. 6 by a kabala dated 31.1.84 (Ext. 2(Ka); that subsequently the said vendor sold the case land by a kabala dated 14.7.84 (Ext.1) to the petitioner No.1 A. Rahim at a consideration of Taka 20,000.00; that the pre-emptors had no knowledge about the said transfer till 1st week of September, 1986; that after obtaining certified copy of the said sale deed on 7.9.86 pre-emptors came to know that the case land was sold by the said vendor to the petitioner No. 1 and petitioner No. 2 disclosed that he was going to purchase the said land from petitioner No. 1; that the pre-emptors being co-sharers in the case plot filed the case on deposit of consideration with statutory compensation. 

 3. Petitioner Nos. 1 and 2 contested the case by filing written objection denying the material allegations and stating, inter alia, that the case is bad for defect of parties and that petitioner No. 1 having sold the case land to the petitioner No. 2 by sale deed dated 24.6.86 (Ext. Ka) he has no subsisting interest in the case land; that petitioner No.1 made substantial improvement of the land and before his sale to the petitioner No. 2 he offered the same to the pre-emptor opposite parties who refused to buy the same due to paucity of fund; that the case is barred under section 85(2) of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act. 

 6. Mr. BK Das, learned Advocate for the petitioners, submitted that Court of appeal below acted illegally in reversing the finding of the trial Court regarding defect of parties relying upon a Single Bench decision reported in 37 DLR 154. He further submitted that court of appeal below was not justified in granting Taka 45,000.00 as improvement costs to the petitioners. In this case there is no dispute that the pre-emptor-opposite parties are co-sharers in the case land and they impleaded the vendor and purchasers of the case land in the pre-emption case. From the khatian Ext. Ga (1) it transpires that Ambar Mia and others are the recorded owners whereas from kabala dated 22.10.81 Ext. 2 (Ka) it appears that common vendors purchased 15 decimals of land of the case plot from one of the recorded tenants. Mahmuda Khatun, wife of Israil Miah. Admittedly those recorded owners and their heirs and successors have not been impleaded in the pre-emption case. But the question is whether they are necessary parties in the case. Sub-section (2) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act provides for impleading all the co-sharer tenants or all the co-sharer-tenants as well as all the contiguous owners as parties in the pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Under sub-section (4) of the said section 96 remaining co-sharer tenants and the contiguous land owners have been given option of rateable pre-emption. Similarly, under sub-section (4) of section 24 of the Non- Agricultural Tenancy Act remaining co-sharer tenants have been given option to pray for rateable pre-emption. But there is no provision in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act similar to sub-section (2) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act Mr. Das strenuously argued that in the case of Hosna Ara Begum and others vs. Musammat Anowara Begum and others reported in 37 DLR 154 the question regarding option of the remaining co-sharers to pray for rateable pre-emption was not noticed and, as such, the said decision is required to be reconsidered. He submits that unless the remaining co-sharer tenants are made parties in a pre-emption case under section 24 of the said Act they would be deprived of the right to pray for rateable pre-emption. This argument though plausible is devoid of any merit. As there is no provision in section 24 of the Non-Agricultural Tenancy Act to implead other co-sharers as party in a pre-emption proceeding it cannot be said that such a case will be bad for defect of party for not impleading the remaining co-sharer tenants. Any co-sharer tenant may apply for pre-emption under section 24 of the said Act by impleading the vendor as well as the purchaser of the disputed sale. In that case remaining co-sharer tenant or tenants may file separate case for pre-emption or pray for rateable pre-emption by being impleaded in the pre-emption case already filed by one of the co-sharers. I, therefore, find nothing to disagree with the said decision which is based on an unreported decision of the Appellate Division. 

 7. It appears from paragraph 19(E) of the written objection that the petitioner No. 1 spent huge amounts for various improvement costs and from paragraph 9(G) that the petitioner No. 2 spent sum of Taka 50,000.00 for construction of boundary wall and other development works. Petitioners No. 1 deposing as OPW 1 stated that he spent Taka 50/60 thousand for earth filling but he is silent about the costs of construction of the boundary wall. In that view of the matter as there is no substantive evidence on record regarding improvement costs I find nothing to interfere with the improvement costs awarded by the learned Court of appeal below after hearing the parties. I, therefore, find no merit in the contention raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner.
